name: Functioning Neuroendocrine Tumor of the Pancreas

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of hormone-related clinical syndrome (e.g., hypoglycemia, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome)
Histological confirmation of neuroendocrine tumor with immunohistochemical staining positive for neuroendocrine markers (chromogranin A, synaptophysin)
Elevated serum levels of specific hormones (insulin, gastrin, glucagon, VIP, somatostatin) corresponding to tumor subtype
Localization of tumor by imaging modalities (CT, MRI, somatostatin receptor scintigraphy, PET)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus clinical syndrome or biochemical evidence of hormone hypersecretion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, histological, and imaging findings.

laboratory: Elevated serum hormone levels specific to tumor subtype (insulin, gastrin, VIP, glucagon, somatostatin)
Hypoglycemia with inappropriately elevated insulin levels (insulinoma)
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI showing pancreatic mass
Somatostatin receptor scintigraphy (Octreoscan) or PET with Ga-68 DOTATATE for tumor localization
Endoscopic ultrasound for fine needle aspiration biopsy
genetic: MEN1 gene mutations in familial cases
Other rare genetic syndromes (e.g., von Hippel-Lindau disease)
other: Histopathology with immunohistochemical staining positive for chromogranin A and synaptophysin
Ki-67 proliferation index for grading tumor aggressiveness

distinguishingFeatures: Often diagnosed incidentally or due to mass effect

redFlags: Severe fasting hypoglycemia with neuroglycopenic symptoms
Refractory peptic ulcer disease with diarrhea
Rapidly progressive weight loss and abdominal mass
